claims.text: High-entropy alloys contain multiple principal elements.
Machine-learning models can account for complex interactions among multiple principal elements in high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning models can capture nonlinear relationships between alloy composition and melting properties.
Capturing nonlinear composition–property relationships will improve the accuracy of melting-property predictions.
The proposed machine-learning intervention will predict melting temperature more accurately than current traditional methods.
The proposed machine-learning intervention will predict other melting properties more accurately than current traditional methods.
The proposed machine-learning intervention will be more computationally efficient than current traditional prediction methods.
A sufficient number of training and validation data points is required for the intervention to remain valid.
The machine-learning models must be properly calibrated and validated for the intervention to remain valid.
Performance may depend on the quality and quantity of training data.
Performance may depend on model architecture and hyperparameter choices.
The hypothesis is restricted to high-entropy alloys with multiple principal elements and may not transfer to other alloy classes.
Predictive performance can be benchmarked using mean absolute error and computational time.
